target_customer: Aerospace and defense programs needing hypersonic reentry testing, and pharma, materials, semiconductor and optics firms wanting microgravity manufacturing
problem: Getting products and test articles back from orbit and hypersonic flight is costly and one-time; reusable spacecraft aim to make it repeatable.
business_model: Microgravity and reentry as a service on reusable ENOS spacecraft

founders.name: Stef Crum
education: PhD in space systems engineering, pursued at Georgia Tech
previous_startups: Da Vinci Satellite (satellite mission non-profit, founded)

founders.name: Will Sherman
prior_employers: DoD (satellite and reentry work, per launch post)
education: Georgia Tech aerospace engineering PhD, dropped out

competitors.name: Varda Space Industries
competitors.what: Orbital microgravity manufacturing capsules recovered after reentry
competitors.traction_then: First of the reentry startups to fly and recover a capsule; founded January 2021

competitors.name: Inversion Space
competitors.what: Reusable cargo reentry capsule (Arc), smaller Ray test vehicle first

competitors.name: Outpost
competitors.funding_then: Later won a $33.2M Air Force STRATFI contract

technical_complexity.rationale: Controlled reentry with precision landing, a free-flying reusable spacecraft and hypersonic thermal protection are hardware and regulatory heavy, and the schedule slipped from early 2026 to later in 2026 per sources.

defensibility.rationale: Reentry vehicle know-how and flight heritage are hard to replicate, but several funded rivals are building similar vehicles.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: SpaceX announced a Starfall demo and several startups pursue reentry; no source shows anyone copying or acquiring Reditus as of late 2026.

market_need_then: Defense interest in hypersonic test targets and reentry testing plus emerging microgravity manufacturing demand; Dawn Aerospace announced a propulsion supply deal in March 2025.

branding.name_origin: Reditus is Latin for return, per a third-party profile; the founders' own explanation was not found.
branding.domain_note: Uses reditus.space; no purchase history found.

identity.logo: Not described by any source found
identity.visual_style: Aerospace look with a launch countdown on the site
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and mission-led, tagline Designed on Earth, Made in Space

branding.brand_signature: The tagline Designed on Earth, Made in Space and the ENOS spacecraft name

brand_strength.rationale: A meaningful Latin name matching the return thesis and a clear tagline, with coverage in trade press, but no evidence the brand itself drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Reditus Space has raised a $7.1M seed and built its ENOS vehicle, with the first flight pushed from early 2026 into later 2026 and the vehicle shipped to Vandenberg by July 2026. Founders with NASA and Space Force backgrounds fit the market, but outcome depends on a successful first reentry.
notes: Seed reported as $7.1M in December 2025 by Hypepotamus and others; aggregators cite totals of $7.6M or $7.8M and one dates it to March 2025, which are unverified. The YC page says first orbital recovery mission Q4 2026 while the launch post gave a window from March 2026. Competitor entries are dated by year only because the source is a 2025 year-in-review; Varda's founding date is from that source.
